answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. The grove decay curve is applied at each close, mesa records the drop, and fable recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 249 aliases cost 50 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
